ember-orange.$description: Ember Orange — Orange supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

vapor-pink.$description: Vapor Pink — Secondary decorative accent — rare highlights, special-emphasis inline marks, and select graphic flourishes. Used as a cool counterpoint to Ember Orange when a second color is needed

parchment.$description: Parchment — Page canvas — the warm off-white that defines the site's light mode. Warmer than pure white, it gives the whole interface a paper-like quality

bone.$description: Bone — Elevated surface — cards, content blocks, nav backgrounds. One step lighter than Parchment, used to lift elements off the canvas without harsh contrast

graphite.$description: Graphite — Primary text and dark section background — near-black with a cool cast. The workhorse color for headings, body copy, and full-bleed dark bands

obsidian.$description: Obsidian — Deepest dark — alt dark-panel fill, footer surfaces. Slightly warmer than Graphite for variation in dark sections

stone.$description: Stone — Secondary text — descriptions, supporting copy, muted labels. Warm olive-gray that harmonizes with Parchment rather than fighting it

ash.$description: Ash — Tertiary text and disabled states — nav dropdown items, fine print, inactive icons

khaki.$description: Khaki — Hairline borders and dividers — low-contrast warm gray that defines edges without drawing attention

mist.$description: Mist — List separators and secondary borders — a touch cooler than Khaki for list-item dividers

space-grotesk.$description: Primary typeface — all headings and body text. Weight 300 for headlines creates a quiet, technical confidence (anti-convention; most sites shout with 700). Weight 400 for body. Tight tracking at -0.02em across all sizes keeps headlines compact even at 46px.

ibm-plex-mono.$description: Eyebrow labels, section tags, code snippets, small data. Tracking +0.1em (wide) gives it a technical-spec or serial-number quality — used sparingly above headings or as status indicators.
